evidence: Ter. And. 3.2.4: mox ego hūc revertor (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 10.4.8: jussit mihi nūntiārī, mox sē ventūrum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Mostly of the future; of the past it is “soon after, then”: mox deinde, soon thereafter. “How soon?” is quam mox?; “too soon”, nimium cito.

evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. brevis: brevī tempore and brevī are classical
terms.comment: Short for brevī tempore, “within a short time”: Brevī redībō, I'll be back soon. It does not mean “for a short time”.

phrases.latin: Quandō rūrsus volābimus? — Mox. Nōndum dīmidium itineris cōnfēcimus.
phrases.english: When will we fly again? — Soon. We haven’t done half the journey yet.

sources: Lewis & Short: mox · Lewis & Short: brevis
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 88, 298, 382, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
